message.content:
**Hydrogen – Key Properties**

| Category | Property | Value / Description |
|----------|----------|---------------------|
| **Basic Atomic Data** | Atomic number | 1 |
| | Atomic mass (average) | 1.008 u |
| | Electron configuration | 1s¹ |
| | Isotopes | H‑1 (protium), H‑2 (deuterium), H‑3 (tritium) |
| | Natural abundance | Protium ≈ 99.98 %, Deuterium ≈ 0.02 %, Tritium negligible |
| **Physical Properties** | State at STP | Gas |
| | Boiling point | –252.9 °C (20.3 K) |
| | Melting point | –259.2 °C (14.0 K) |
| | Density (gas, STP) | 0.08988 g L⁻¹ |
| | Density (liquid, 20 K) | 0.0708 g cm⁻³ |
| | Molar volume (gas, STP) | 22.414 L mol⁻¹ |
| | Specific heat (gas, 25 °C) | 28.8 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ |
| | Thermal conductivity (gas, 25 °C) | 0.180 W m⁻¹ K⁻¹ |
| | Sound speed (gas, 25 °C) | 1275 m s⁻¹ |
| **Chemical Properties** | Electronegativity (Pauling) | 2.20 |
| | First ionization energy | 13.598 eV |
| | Electron affinity | –0.754 eV |
| | Standard enthalpy of formation (H₂(g)) | 0 kJ mol⁻¹ (by definition) |
| | Standard Gibbs free energy of formation (H₂(g)) | 0 kJ mol⁻¹ |
| | Standard entropy (H₂(g)) | 130.68 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ |
| | Oxidation states | +1 (as H⁺), –1 (as hydride H⁻) |
| | Common compounds | H₂O, H₂SO₄, HCl, NH₃, CH₄, etc. |
| | Bond dissociation energy (H–H) | 436 kJ mol⁻¹ |
| | Acid–base behavior | Acts as a proton donor (H⁺) in aqueous solution; forms hydronium H₃O⁺ |
| | Redox behavior | Strong reducing agent (especially in the form of H₂ gas or hydride ions) |
| **Isotopic Differences** | Deuterium (²H) | 2 u, heavier, lower zero‑point energy → stronger bonds, higher melting/boiling points |
| | Tritium (³H) | 3 u, radioactive (β‑decay, half‑life ≈ 12.32 y) |
| | Isotopic effects | Deuterated solvents (D₂O) have higher boiling point (+7 °C) and lower dielectric constant |
| **Spectroscopic Features** | Rotational spectrum | Microwave absorption at ~ 1420 MHz (21 cm line) – key in radio astronomy |
| | Vibrational frequency (H₂) | ~ 4401 cm⁻¹ |
| | Electronic transitions | UV absorption at ~ 121.6 nm (Lyman‑α line) |
| **Astrophysical Role** | Stellar fusion | Proton–proton chain, deuterium burning, tritium fusion in early universe |
| | Cosmic background | 21 cm line used to map neutral hydrogen in galaxies |
| | Interstellar medium | Dominant component of molecular clouds (H₂) |
| **Safety & Handling** | Flammability | Extremely flammable; explosive limits 4–75 % (v/v) in air |
| | Toxicity | Non‑toxic, but can cause asphyxiation in confined spaces |
| | Storage | Requires high‑pressure cylinders or cryogenic tanks; special precautions for cryogenic temperatures |
| **Applications** | Fuel cell technology | Hydrogen fuel cells produce electricity + water |
| | Chemical industry | Production of ammonia (Haber process), methanol, hydrogenation reactions |
| | Space propulsion | Liquid hydrogen + liquid oxygen as rocket propellant |
| | Metallurgy | Hydrogen embrittlement in steels; used in hydrogen reduction processes |
| | Analytical chemistry | Used as a reducing agent in chromatography, as a carrier gas in mass spectrometry |
| **Miscellaneous** | Hydrogen bonding | H atoms can form hydrogen bonds (e.g., in water, alcohols) |
| | Quantum effects | Zero‑point energy significant due to low mass; leads to tunneling in reactions |
| | Environmental impact | Clean combustion (water vapor); potential for large‑scale energy storage |

---

### Quick Takeaways

- **Lightest element**: Atomic number 1, mass ~1 u.
- **Highly reactive**: Forms H⁺ (proton) and H⁻ (hydride) species.
- **Two stable isotopes**: Protium (most common) and deuterium (stable, heavier); tritium is radioactive.
- **Key in energy**: Fuel cells, rocket propellants, hydrogenation chemistry.
- **Astrophysical marker**: 21 cm line maps neutral hydrogen across the cosmos.
- **Safety note**: Extremely flammable; requires careful handling.

Feel free to ask for deeper dives into any specific property or application!
